11–12 Sketch the solid described by the given inequalities.

problem.paragraph: $$r^{2} \leqslant z \leqslant 8 - r^{2}$$
$$0 \leqslant \theta \leqslant \pi/2$$ , $$r \leqslant z \leqslant 2$$

A cylindrical shell is $$20$$ cm long, with inner radius $$6$$ cm and outer radius $$7$$ cm. Write inequalities that describe the shell in an appropriate coordinate system. Explain how you have positioned the coordinate system with respect to the shell.
Use graphing software to draw the solid enclosed by the paraboloids $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and $$z = 5 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ .

exercises.instruction: 15–16 Express the triple integral $$\iiint_{E}(x,y,z)\mathit{dV}$$ as an iterated integral in cylindrical coordinates for the given function $$f$$ and solid region $$E$$ . Evaluate the iterated integral.

image.alt: Details A solid is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The solid, labeled E, resembles a half paraboloid mounted on top of a half cylinder. The half cylinder part is labeled x^2 + y^2 = 1 and its semicircular base lies on the x y plane with its center at the origin. The rectangular surface of the half cylinder lies on the x z plane. The half paraboloid, labeled z = 2 minus x^2 minus y^2, has its vertex on the positive z axis, opens downward with its rim on the top side of the half cylinder. The vertical side of the half paraboloid lies on the x z plane.

problem.paragraph: $$f(x,y,z) = xy$$

image.alt: Details A solid is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The solid, labeled E, resembles a paraboloid mounted on an inverted cone. The cone, labeled z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), has its tip at the origin and opens upward with its circular base parallel to the x y plane and the center of the base lies on the positive z axis. The paraboloid, labeled z = 6 minus x^2 minus y^2, has its vertex on the positive z axis, opens downward, with its rim resting on the rim of the circular base of the cone. A vertical trace drawn on the surface of the solid lies on the x z plane and resembles a parabola opening downward resting on a v shaped curve.

exercises.instruction: 17–18 Sketch the solid whose volume is given by the integral and evaluate the integral.

problem.paragraph: $$\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}{\int_{0}^{3}{\int_{r^{2}}^{9}{r\mathit{dz}\mathit{dr}d\theta}}}$$
$$\int_{0}^{2}{\int_{0}^{2\pi}{\int_{0}^{r}{r\mathit{dz}d\theta\mathit{dr}}}}$$
Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is the region that lies inside the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 16$$ and between the planes $$z = - 5$$ and $$z = 4$$ .
Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}{z\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is enclosed by the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and the plane $$z = 4$$ .
Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}{{\left( {x + y + z} \right)}\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is the solid in the first octant that lies under the paraboloid $$z = 4 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ .

Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}{{\left( {x - y} \right)}\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is the solid that lies between the cylinders $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ and $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 16$$ , above the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane, and below the plane $$z = y + 4$$ .
Evaluate $$\iiint_{E}{x^{2}\mathit{dV}}$$ , where $$E$$ is the solid that lies within the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ , above the plane $$z = 0$$ , and below the cone $$z^{2} = 4x^{2} + 4y^{2}$$ .
Find the volume of the solid that lies within both the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ and the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 4$$ .
Find the volume of the solid that is enclosed by the cone $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ and the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 2$$ .
Find the volume of the solid that lies between the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and the sphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 2$$ .

list.item: Find the volume of the region $$E$$ that lies between the paraboloid $$z = 24 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ and the cone $$z = 2\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ .
Find the centroid of $$E$$ (the center of mass in the case where the density is constant).
Find the volume of the solid that the cylinder $$r = a\cos\theta$$ cuts out of the sphere of radius $$a$$ centered at the origin.
Illustrate the solid of part (a) by graphing the sphere and the cylinder on the same screen.

problem.paragraph: Find the mass and center of mass of the solid $$S$$ bounded by the paraboloid $$z = 4x^{2} + 4y^{2}$$ and the plane $$z = a{\left( {a > 0} \right)}$$ if $$S$$ has constant density $$K$$ .
Find the mass of a ball $$B$$ given by $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leqslant a^{2}$$ if the density at any point is proportional to its distance from the $$z$$ -axis.

exercises.instruction: 31–32 Evaluate the integral by changing to cylindrical coordinates.

problem.paragraph: $$\int_{- 2}^{2}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - y^{2}}}^{\sqrt{4 - y^{2}}}{\int_{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}^{2}{xz\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}}}}$$

When studying the formation of mountain ranges, geologists estimate the amount of work required to lift a mountain from sea level. Consider a mountain that is essentially in the shape of a right circular cone. Suppose that the weight density of the material in the vicinity of a point $$P$$ is $$g(P)$$ and the height is $$h(P)$$ .

list.item: Find a definite integral that represents the total work done in forming the mountain.

Assume that Mount Fuji in Japan is in the shape of a right circular cone with radius $$62,000$$ ft, height $$12,400$$ ft, and density a constant $$200{lb}/{ft}^{3}$$ . How much work was done in forming Mount Fuji if the land was initially at sea level? S.R. Lee Photo Traveller/Shutterstock.ocm
